(1) the similarity between two sets of terms is not always a function of their size and (2) a metric for calculating the similarity between two concepts should be based on a set of properties of those concepts and on the relations between them, and not only on a set of relations between the two concepts.

we designed and implemented two novel algorithms, called “Similarity by Conceptual Distance” and “Similarity by Semantic Distance”, for measuring the similarity between sets (i.e., the semantic distance between sets of concepts) belonging to the same domain ontology.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the design and development of an ontology-based similarity between sets of semantic concepts, that is, concepts belonging to a given ontology, and with the application of such a similarity to the field of agent technology.
the following issues: (i) how to define a similarity measure between two sets of elements that belong to the same ontology, and (ii) how to implement it in order to make it computationally tractable.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have defined and implemented two new similarity metrics between sets of concepts, that take advantage of the structure of the ontology and of the semantics of its relations.

we have designed and developed a new algorithm for the calculation of the semantic distance between a pair of concepts belonging to an ontology, based on the number of common subsumers, and two algorithms for the calculation of similarity between two sets of concept belonging to a common reference ontology.

we propose two new algorithms, that we have called “conceptual distance” and “conceptual overlap” algorithms, respectively, for calculating the similarity between sets and concepts taken from the same ontology O.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, if we want our agents to act as “digital personal assistants”, we should provide them with more complex metrics for evaluating the semantic distance between sets of concepts, in order to better reflect our common sense reasoning.

the similarity between two sets of concept can be computed by using two different metrics: the first one takes into account only the number of shared concepts, while the second metric takes into account both the number of shared and non-shared concepts.
the similarity between two sets of elements can be calculated by considering the similarity between each pair of corresponding elements.
